title: Current public large-load source context — 2026-09-27
purpose: Dated control-plane snapshot of the principal public market and utility source systems used by the registry. This is source context, not a substitute for row-level records.

sources.current_context: The registry retains a complete current public queue snapshot and separate historical cluster-series records. Historical serial/cluster versioning remains a distinct research task.
The registry retains 3,873 current queue records and an explicit 153-row >=100 MW unlocated worklist. Missing public location fields are preserved as missing rather than geocoded.

PJM's current Large Load page says the Large Load Registry is pending FERC approval, the new existing/future registry tool is expected Jan. 1, 2027, and aggregated public registry information is expected in March 2027. Current serial/cycle service-request data remain the public interim source.

ERCOT's September 2026 public materials document Batch Zero eligibility verification RFIs and a State & Community Impact RFI. The Large Load Integration page states RIOO portal responses are the controlling documents.
SPP publicly maintains a High Impact Large Load process and has September 17, 2026 public meeting materials. The public active GI queue is retained separately.

The official Interconnection Queue workbook is the public queue source used by the registry; the current repository still needs a fresh successful workbook capture before a current complete row-level export can be asserted.
The registry preserves the public external-queue source family and named large-load forecast/project evidence; project-specific milestones require document-level extraction.
AESO says it publishes all projects following its Connection Process monthly, with Excel, map, GIS shapefile and KML resources. The latest published list is dated Sep. 1, 2026.
The public Application Status universe is retained; later technical-feasibility details can be confidential. IESO's large-computational-load technical requirements were revised Sep. 3, 2026.
BC Hydro publicly reported 15 Emerging Industries applications representing close to 800 MW and said feasibility results would be provided by Aug. 24, 2026.

Hydro-Québec reported nearly 190 MW of peak data-centre consumption under the discussed rate and said sector peak consumption could reach approximately 1,000 MW by 2035. This is sector context, not facility attribution.
Manitoba Hydro publishes large-supply request requirements above 5 MW, including legal entity, site, construction timing, operation schedule, peak MW and annual GWh.
Alectra's Vaughan MTS No. 6 project page describes a proposed 230 kV station with 170 MVA capacity supporting a proposed 108 MVA data-centre facility for an undisclosed customer.

semantics: Status is dated 2026-09-27. A public source being active does not imply every customer/application record is public. Confidential or restricted data remains out of the registry unless independently disclosed.
